text:
B: Hiya! Oh, I was hoping I'd get you. I'm Nicola.
A: Hello. Nusrat.
B: I said on your photo, I bet she's the one who keeps the group on track. Sorry, is that cheeky?
A: No. It's probably accurate.
B: Ha! Where are you, love?
A: Ilford.
B: Oh, not far, I'm Eltham. So go on, what do you do? I've got a feeling it's something with numbers.
A: Management accountant, at a housing association in Stratford. Budget reports, mostly.
B: Oh, I knew it. I work in a primary school office. Front desk, attendance, dinner money. Not quite the same level.
A: My son's in Year One. Can I ask you something, then?
B: Course you can.
A: Why do schools keep changing the date for parents' evening? His has moved twice this term. I'd already booked the time off.
B: Oh, I'm so sorry, that's honestly one of the things I get shouted at about most. Nine times out of ten it's because a teacher's off, or there's a training day that's moved, or the hall's double-booked for something. And the office are usually the last to know, I'll be honest with you. We find out the same morning the letter goes out.
A: So it's poor planning.
B: Erm, yeah. Sort of, yeah. I can't really argue with that.
A: At least you're honest about it.
B: Well, there's no point pretending, is there? What I'd do is email the office and ask them to confirm it in writing. It gives them a bit of a nudge.
A: That's useful. Thank you.
B: Is he enjoying it, Year One?
A: Yes. He likes phonics. He reads the cereal box to me every morning.
B: Oh, bless him. Mine are grown up now, twenty-seven and twenty-four. I miss that bit, the cereal box bit.
A: Do they live near?
B: My daughter's in Dartford, my son's in Manchester. We're going up to see him soon, actually. I keep checking the trains like a mad woman.
A: I'd book them early. And I'd check the connections twice.
B: Oh, Steve says that! He thinks I'm disorganised. I'm not, I'm just disorganised at home. At work I've got everything on a spreadsheet.
A: What do you use?
B: Excel, mainly. I did an evening course at the school. I can do a filter and a, erm, the one that adds things up, sum. I don't know the fancy stuff, I'll be honest.
A: XLOOKUP would save you a lot of time with attendance. Matching names across two lists.
B: Sorry, X what? You'll have to write that down for me.
A: XLOOKUP. It's not difficult. Ten minutes on YouTube.
B: Right, I'm writing it on my hand. Steve'll think I've joined a cult. So what do you do to relax then, after all that?
A: A crime novel, usually. Or a Korean drama after he's asleep.
B: Oh, I do a crime drama! My book club's just done a thriller and we argued for an hour about the ending. Do you ever...
